findings.where: Screens 9 and 10, the caption under the picture, and the practice rules
findings.what: The rule 'B in mT = 0.2 × A ÷ mm' is used as a constant, but no source in the lesson or in research-notes.md states it (the notes only have OpenStax's contents line '12.2 Magnetic Field Due to a Thin Straight Wire', and its K.check has no source), so add a quote for B = μ0 I ÷ (2π r), or a cited μ0 = 4π × 10⁻⁷ with the 0.2 worked out on screen.

findings.where: Caption under the picture, shown on all 12 screens
findings.what: 'Each line drawn is 1 µWb' is false on the wire screens (1, 2, 9, 10), where the rings are drawn at steps of density (0.05 × √2ⁿ mT), and on the loop and coil screens (3, 12), where the lines number turns × current ÷ 10, so in a lesson about telling flux from density it labels density contours as flux; show it only on the hoop screens (5 to 8, 11).

The rule that a wire's field falls in step with distance is stated with no reason, so add one plain sentence, such as 'a ring twice as far out is twice as long, so the same current's field is spread twice as thin round it'.

The Turns slider appears the moment the picture switches from Loop to Coil, which pushes the Current slider and the Back and Continue row down partway through the demonstration; keep its space from the start, or show it disabled on Loop.

findings.where: End of the lesson (screen 12 and the finish text)
findings.what: The brief promised a last screen that puts iron in the coil and leaves lesson 2 to ask why the flux jumps, and that names contactors, relays and solenoids as where the field is used; neither is on any screen (the uses appear only in the practice text), so add a closing line or a run after screen 12.

The field lines that loop round each row of turns are drawn through the circles of the end conductors (top-left and top-right dots, bottom-left and bottom-right crosses); start or clip those lines outside the conductor rings.

At 360 px the lead breaks '5' from 'mT' across two lines because it uses a plain space, and it gives '10 A in the wire' although screens 9 and 10 use 20 A; use a non-breaking space and say the values are examples without tying them to one screen.

'It is the flux per square metre, square-on, in teslas, T.' stacks three comma asides in one sentence; split it, for example 'It is the flux through each square metre, square-on. It is measured in teslas, T.'

For the first 2.7 s the top of the picture is an empty band about 80 px tall, waiting for the grip panel to fade in, so the opening view is text, a gap, then bare needles at 'No current'; fade the panel in from the start of the current's rise, or move the needles up.
